scenes.text: [A] I wake up in the middle of the night. Sam’s still sleeping. She was up later than me, waiting for Mom and Halmoni. I don’t know if they came home.

[B] And I can’t stand not knowing. I can’t stand feeling helpless—like I have to fix it, but I don’t know how. [C] Quietly I walk downstairs. Mom’s sleeping on the couch, and I crack Halmoni’s door open.

Inside, she’s wrapped in a cocoon of silk sheets, and I feel dizzy with relief. Halmoni’s okay. I press my hand against the wall to keep from tipping over. I want to go to her, but the image of her in the road burns in my brain.
Leftover fear sits in my chest. [D] For now, it’s enough just to know she’s all right. So I shut the door. [E] As I do, the house groans, shattering the silent night.

Shadows dance around me. [F] And from behind me, someone says, “Hello, Lily.” It’s a gravelly female voice. It scrapes against my ears like claws on rice paper. “I’ve been searching for your family for a long, long time.”

[G] I spin around, trying to find the source of the voice. [H] But there’s nobody else in the room except for Mom, who’s still sleeping. [I] My rabbit heart panics, pounding against my ribs like it wants to escape. [J] “Oh, come on now.

I’m not that scary.” The voice seems to come from all around me—from inside me, even. It echoes in my chest. [A] The shadows in the kitchen start to take shape, shifting and stretching. And then they come together, forming one shape.

The giant shadow steps forward, into the starlight, and it becomes the tiger—big as a car, filling the whole hallway. [B] “You talk,” I whisper. And then, without meaning to, I add, “And you’re a girl.” [C] I clamp my lips shut, because what a ridiculous thing to say.
[D] She scoffs. “Typical. You hear one story about a male tiger and think we’re all the same? Humans are the worst.”

[E] She takes a step toward me and I press myself back. My shoulder blades dig into Halmoni’s door. [F] Maybe I’m trapped in an elaborate dream—but I don’t think so. I feel the chill in the air, the brush of goose bumps on my arm, the warped wood beneath my feet, and the pinch in my shoulders as I press them back.
[G] Dreams are not made of details. Are nightmares? [H] I glance over at Mom on the couch, but she just snores. [I] “Don’t worry,” the tiger says.
“Your mother won’t be bothering us.” [J] My whole body clenches, but the tiger rolls her eyes. “She’s a heavy sleeper.” [K] A not-small part of my brain is screaming, You are talking to a tiger!
A tiger is talking to you. This is for-sure impossible. [L] I feel a little dizzy. “Go away,” I tell her.
[A] The tiger steps closer, tail swishing back and forth. She tilts her head and flicks an ear. “Why so hostile, Little Egg? I am not going to eat you, just so you know.
I’m on a kimchi diet.” [B] I stare at her. This is the monster Halmoni warned me about. [C] She makes a sound that’s halfway between a purr and a growl.
“Your halmoni stole the stars, and I am here to collect them. That is all. Will you help me, little one?” [D] My mouth is so dry, I can barely form the word, but I manage.
“No.” [E] She sighs. “You humans understand so little of the world, and your halmoni can’t see what she’s done. She doesn’t see what’s harming her.
I only want to help her. Trust me.” [F] I shake my head, because Halmoni told me not to trust tigers. And it’s pretty clear that the tiger is harming her.

The tiger was in the road when Halmoni got sick. The tiger scared her. [G] But the big cat continues, “Story magic is powerful, powerful enough to change someone. And when a story is locked away, its magic only grows.
Sometimes it grows sour. The magic becomes a kind of poison. Do you understand?” [H] I refuse to respond.

I won’t let her twist lies around my heart. [I] “Lily Bean, if you return those stories to me, your halmoni will feel better. If they stay locked away, they will make her sick. They will”—her teeth flash—“eat her up.”

[J] “You’re lying,” I say, but my voice cracks. [A] “I’m offering a deal. You help me find the stories, I’ll return them to their place in the sky, and you never have to think about them again. I get my stars back, and we help your halmoni.

You don’t even have to hear the stories. Everybody wins.” The tiger shifts her weight, paw to paw, and her fur glistens in the starlight. “Don’t you want to be a hero?” [B] Here’s the scariest part: something deep inside me says yes.

I am never the hero—not like Halmoni—and part of me wants to be. [C] I bite my lip so my yes won’t escape. [D] “You should know”—her voice is so deep it vibrates through me—“this is your one chance to help your halmoni. I won’t offer again.”

[E] Halmoni told me to be careful, and just the thought of making a deal with the tiger rips my stomach to shreds. But there’s so much Halmoni didn’t tell me. There’s so much she’s kept hidden—so much I want to know. [F] What if the tiger’s right?
What if these stolen star stories are making Halmoni sick? [G] I am frozen, trapped in my own thoughts. This is my problem. This is why Sam calls me a QAG.
I’m so afraid of saying the wrong answer that I don’t say anything at all. [H] For a few stretched-out moments, the tiger waits. Then she shakes her head. Already she’s fading into shadow.
“I was hoping you’d surprise me.” [I] I think of Halmoni tonight, and how helpless I felt, and how I need to fix this. “Wait!” I call out. “I’ll do it!”
[J] But I’m too late. Her stripes blur into blackness, and she’s gone.
